q: Virudhachalam ceramic and refractory kilns burn firewood, coal, petcoke and RPO: what is the cluster's footprint?
title: Virudhachalam kilns: four fuels, one footprint
short: TERI counted about 300 small and micro units near Virudhachalam making about 60,000 t a year, using 10,079 toe in 2015, 99% of it kiln fuel. Firewood was the biggest share, then imported coal, petcoke and rubber process oil. Fossil CO2 comes to roughly 23,000 t, about 0.39 t per tonne, with wood CO2 reported separately.
audience: Ceramic, terracotta and refractory units and kiln owners in the Virudhachalam (Vriddhachalam) cluster, Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu

sections.h: Each kiln type has its own fuel
ul: Tunnel kilns, 5: three fire ceramics on RPO or LDO at about 7.5 tpd; two fire high alumina refractory bricks on petcoke and imported coal dust at about 20 tpd.
Shuttle kilns, 20: batch firing of toys and art ware on RPO.
Downdraft kilns, about 100 built, about 20 still firing: wood, mainly for the bottom boring sets steel plants buy.

sections.h: Heat per kg tells you which kiln to fix

p: Firewood 18,000 t (4,140 toe), imported coal 4,800 t (3,360 toe), petcoke 1,440 t (1,267 toe), RPO 1,316 kL (1,211 toe) and 1.18 million kWh of TANGEDCO power (102 toe). Downdraft kilns took 41% of the energy and rotary kilns 34%. Energy was about half of production cost. A refractory tunnel kiln unit used about 644 toe a year; a shuttle kiln toy unit about 41.

sections.h: What cuts fuel, and by how much
ul: Lighter tunnel kiln cars with hollow ceramic pipes, fibre blankets and cordierite blocks: about 3% of heat input, 52 toe a year across the cluster.
Automatic air to fuel control and better burners on tunnel and shuttle kilns: about 3%, 178 toe.
Combustion air preheating from shuttle kiln flue gas at 900 to 1,000 °C: about 7%, 57 toe.
Moving downdraft work into continuous kilns is the big step: a downdraft kiln uses about 2.4 times the heat per kg of a tunnel kiln.

example.title: Estimate: cluster CO2 by fuel
lines: Imported coal: 3,360 toe x 41.868 GJ x 94.6 kg CO2 per GJ = about 13,300 t
Petcoke: 1,267 toe x 41.868 x 97.5 = about 5,200 t
RPO, taken as fuel oil: 1,211 toe x 41.868 x 77.4 = about 3,900 t
Power: 1.18 million kWh x 0.675 = about 800 t; fossil total about 23,200 t, or 0.39 t per tonne of 60,000 t
Firewood, biogenic and reported separately: 4,140 toe x 41.868 x 112 = about 19,400 t
example.note: An estimate using IPCC 2006 default factors and the CEA FY 2025-26 grid factor; RPO has no IPCC default of its own. Use your own fuel invoices and test reports.

senseible: Senseible reads RPO, coal, petcoke and wood purchase invoices and TANGEDCO bills into a monthly record for your unit, keeping wood as biogenic, so you have your own figure per tonne when a steel plant or exporter asks.
